sections.h2: See Your Clothing on a Virtual Model
paras: Put your clothing on a lifelike virtual model and launch your next collection faster, without arranging a new shoot.

sections.h2: Launch the Set Without a Casting Day
paras: Lining up a model, a photographer, and a stylist slows every drop. One delay can push the whole set.
Upload the clothing photos you have. A realistic virtual model wears the outfit, so you can preview the set and update the listing in minutes.
sections.alt: Adult woman with short copper hair wearing a plain gray hoodie on an autumn city sidewalk.

sections.h2: Start From a Flat Photo or a Hanger Shot
paras: Use a photo of someone already wearing the piece, or a simple flat lay. Lay the hoodie flat, or hang it, and shoot the front in daylight.
Creases in that photo can become odd folds on the person. Get the sleeves, the hem, and the collar in frame. If the first shot is soft, retake it before you open the [photo tools](page:photo-hub).
sections.alt: Hands smooth a plain gray hoodie beside a wooden hanger on a light surface.

sections.h2: Keep One Face Across Every Channel
paras: Save the virtual model you like and reuse that person, so the set looks like one shoot instead of a new studio every time.
Use that saved person on the product page, on a [marketplace listing](page:plat-amazon), and on an [Instagram post](page:plat-instagram). Clothing, jewelry, and eyewear can share the look.

sections.h2: Use the Same Path for Jewelry and Eyewear
paras: Use a close, sharp photo on a plain surface. Keep the clasp, the stones, and the chain easy to see. Save the person if the next piece should match.
A short line is enough: a close side view, hair back, soft window light. In the result, count the stones and check the clasp.

sections.h2: Show the Fit, the Drape, and the Fabric
paras: Let shoppers see your garment's fit, drape, and material details on a lifelike virtual model before they buy.

Compare the neckline, the length, the print, and the zipper with the real garment. The picture helps a shopper see the drape. It does not replace your measurements. The same file can also feed [ad images](page:social-ad-photos).
sections.alt: Adult East Asian man checking the sleeve and hem of a plain gray hoodie in a fitting room.

sections.h2: Build the Whole Color Set Together
paras: When one garment comes in more than one color, run them with the same saved model and the same scene. Review every file before it goes up.

Pair the worn photo with a flat photo from the [photo tools](page:photo-hub), a room from [lifestyle photos](page:lifestyle-photos), and a plain backdrop from the [background tool](page:change-background). A second color can start from the [color variant](page:tpl-color). [Fashion listings](page:ind-fashion-clothing) can use the same set.

faq.q: Can I show my clothing on an AI model?
faq.a: Yes. Use your garment photo to show the item on a generated adult model. Choose the pose and setting for your listing or lookbook.

faq.q: How does a flat clothing photo become an on-model picture?
faq.a: Upload a clear photo of the whole garment and choose a virtual model. The tool creates an on-model image in minutes without a studio shoot.

faq.q: Can I make on-model photos for a whole catalog?
faq.a: Yes. Send many garment photos through the API and make an image for each product. This saves studio time as your catalog grows.

faq.q: What photo should I start from for clothing or jewelry?
faq.a: Start with a clear photo showing the whole item and its details. A flat lay or hanger photo works for clothing, with no reshoot needed.

faq.q: Do I need to say the person in the photo is generated?
faq.a: Follow the current disclosure rules for the store or ad platform where you post. Add a label when that channel requires one.

faq.q: How many credits does one on-model photo use?
faq.a: One on-model photo costs 24 credits. Starter costs $24.50 for 200 credits, Pro costs $35 for 300, and Premium costs $63 for 600.

faq.q: Can one saved face stay through the whole lookbook?
faq.a: Yes. Reuse the same saved model for each lookbook photo. That gives your collection a consistent face without booking a shoot.

faq.q: How close is an on-model photo to a studio shoot?
faq.a: On-model images can look like studio photos with natural poses and lighting. Check the real garment’s fit and details before publishing.
